title: Ulyana and the Alibi
premise: Tamsin Crane, archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, is hired by a nervous stranger to document that a murder has not yet occurred — the murder of Ulyana Voss, whose body will supposedly be found in the locked crypt within a month. When Ulyana turns up alive but terrified, and then a different body appears in the crypt anyway, Tamsin realizes the client's 'alibi' was a rehearsal: someone using the archive itself to stage a perfect, pre-documented crime. As Tamsin decodes twenty years of their own filing system being quietly rewritten, they discover the killer is someone who helped build it — and that proving an innocence that hasn't happened yet means becoming an accomplice to the truth. In the end Tamsin traps the killer inside the crypt with the falsified record, choosing truth over the loyalty of old friends, at the cost of the archive's sanctity and their own clean hands.
about_author: Emrys Eriksen is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing documents no one was meant to read. They write mysteries about people who mistake order for safety.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A gray-eyed stranger arrives at the archive office with cash and an odd commission: prove, in writing, that Ulyana Voss will not be murdered in the crypt on the winter solstice. Tamsin refuses, then finds the fee already deposited. The beat is unease — a professional's pride pricked by a puzzle too strange to leave alone.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of the Dead
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Establishing the cathedral archive: burial registers, crypt keys, twenty years of the town's secrets filed by Tamsin's own hand. They pull Ulyana Voss's file and find it disturbingly thin — recently thinned. Emotional beat: the first crack in Tamsin's faith in their own records.

chapters.title: Ulyana, Living
chapters.summary: Tamsin tracks down Ulyana Voss, expecting a ghost, and finds a woman very much alive who goes white at the mention of the solstice. She claims never to have hired anyone. POV alternates between Tamsin and Ulyana. Beat: two liars recognizing each other's craft.

chapters.title: What the Crypt Keeps
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, twenty years back: a night in the crypt she has never told anyone about, a death ruled accidental, and a promise extracted from her by three others present. Beat: guilt preserved like a specimen — memory as unreliable archive.

chapters.title: The Client Vanishes
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The gray-eyed stranger cannot be found; the deposit traces to a shell account opened with Tamsin's own office address. Detective Inspector Rhys Calloway takes Tamsin's statement and treats them as either witness or suspect. Beat: the archivist becomes an entry in someone else's file.

chapters.title: Solstice
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge on the night in question. Nothing happens — until dawn, when the sexton finds the crypt locked from inside and a body within: not Ulyana, but Father Anselm, one of the three from Ulyana's past. Beat: dread fulfilled in the wrong shape.

chapters.title: A Perfect Record
chapters.summary: Calloway's POV. The investigation hits a wall: the crypt's lock unpicked without marks, Anselm's death dated hours before anyone entered. Tamsin realizes the murder matches, detail for detail, a hypothetical scenario outlined in the stranger's commission letter. Beat: horror of seeing fiction made flesh.

chapters.title: The Second Set of Hands
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Someone has been borrowing archive materials and returning them microseconds altered — a date here, an initial there. Tamsin reconstructs the tampering pattern and recognizes the handling habits: this person learned filing from Tamsin themselves. Beat: betrayal in one's own handwriting.

chapters.title: The Three Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Of the four present in the crypt twenty years ago, one is dead. The others: Verity Marsh, now a town councilor, and Brother Edric, the cathedral's bell-ringer. Ulyana begins receiving pages from her own old confession, cut into ransom-note fragments. Beat: the past demanding interest.

chapters.title: Verity's Version
chapters.summary: Verity Marsh's POV. A polished, self-justifying account of the old death — self-defense, she insists, an accident covered up to protect the cathedral. She warns Tamsin off with genuine warmth and genuine menace. Beat: loyalty as a cage built by all four together.

chapters.title: Edric Rings True
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Brother Edric, dying of a heart condition, confesses to Tamsin that he wrote the old report falsifying the death — and that his copy of the true record went into the archive, misfiled on purpose, findable only by its creator. Beat: a dying man entrusting truth to the keeper of lies.

chapters.title: Misfiled
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, alone through the night stacks. Following Edric's private logic, Tamsin finds the hidden true record: Anselm killed Verity's husband in self-defense, and the four buried the truth to save the cathedral's name. But the record names a fifth witness — one Tamsin has met. Beat: vertigo as the map redraws itself.

chapters.title: The Gray-Eyed Stranger
chapters.summary: Reveal chapter, Tamsin's POV. The client is the child of Verity's husband — raised abroad, returned under an assumed name, hiring Tamsin not to prevent a murder but to create a documented alibi for one already planned. Tamsin confronts them; they escape, leaving the commission letter's final page behind. Beat: the hunter learning they were bait.

chapters.title: Which Murder
chapters.summary: Calloway and Tamsin pool knowledge uneasily. The remaining target must be Verity or Ulyana — but the tampered files point both directions, deliberately. Tamsin realizes the killer is using the archive as a weapon: whoever reads the record next will be steered. Beat: paranoia; even truth is now a loaded instrument.

chapters.title: Ulyana Runs
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Convinced she is the intended victim, Ulyana flees town, sending Tamsin her fragmentary confession as insurance. On the road she realizes too late that running places her outside every witness's protection. Beat: survival instinct curdling into isolation.

chapters.title: The Archive Burns
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Fire guts the east stacks; the true record survives only because Tamsin broke protocol and took it home. Among the ashes: evidence the fire was set with keys only cathedral staff hold. Beat: grief for twenty years of work — and cold clarity about how small the circle of suspects is.

chapters.title: Verity's Alibi
chapters.summary: Verity's POV. She builds herself an airtight public innocence while privately contacting the gray-eyed stranger — we see she knows who they are, and believes she can buy them as she once bought silence. Beat: the architect of the old cover-up attempting one last renovation.

chapters.title: The Trap in the Filing
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Knowing the killer reads the archive like scripture, Tamsin plants a false record — a fabricated ledger placing the surviving true document in the crypt, timed for the anniversary night. They tell only Calloway, and not all of it. Beat: the archivist committing their first deliberate falsehood.

chapters.title: Anniversary
chapters.summary: Night in the cathedral, multiple POVs converging again. Verity comes for the document; the gray-eyed stranger comes for Verity; Ulyana, summoned by a forged note in Tamsin's hand, walks into the middle. Beat: every debt arriving at once, in the dark, among the bones.

chapters.title: Locked From Inside
chapters.summary: Climax, Tamsin's POV. In the crypt, the stranger forces Verity to confess on tape; Verity turns the moment into an attack; Ulyana chooses testimony over flight. Tamsin seals the crypt from outside — echoing the original murder scene — and holds the door until Calloway arrives. Beat: terror transfigured into resolve; the price paid in full.

chapters.title: Exhibits
chapters.summary: Resolution, Calloway's POV. Verity charged in the old death and the new conspiracy; the stranger's alibi scheme collapses against Tamsin's planted record, which they voluntarily disavow. Ulyana testifies and leaves town lighter than she arrived. Beat: justice administered imperfectly, but administered.

chapters.title: Recatalogued
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, coda. Rebuilding the burned archive, Tamsin files the whole affair honestly — including their own forgery — in a new drawer labeled plainly, without alphabet or code. The last line: some things should be easy to find. Beat: quiet redemption; memory kept, finally, without locks.
